outsideDelete.title: Notes deleted outside Loom Loom
outsideDelete.checking: Changes made outside Loom Loom were found. Checking them — please wait until this finishes.
outsideDelete.intro: These notes were deleted outside Loom Loom (the file explorer, another app or a sync), but parts of the project still depend on them. Choose what to do with each one before carrying on.
outsideDelete.putBackDesc: brings the note back exactly as it was.
outsideDelete.restoreFromTrashDesc: moves the note back out of the vault's trash folder.
outsideDelete.keepTextDesc: for a scene, act or chapter: leaves its text in the script or book. The note itself is made again, but without what was on it (relationships, notes).
outsideDelete.removeTextDesc: for a scene, act or chapter: removes its text from the script or book, removes references to it from other notes, and turns links to it into plain text.
outsideDelete.linkToDesc: points everything that referred to it at another note instead — for a note that was renamed or replaced.
outsideDelete.linkToPick: Pick the {type} it should point to
outsideDelete.cleanUpDesc: removes references to it from other notes, and turns links to it into plain text.
outsideDelete.checkAgainDesc: looks again after you've put a note back yourself, for example from the system trash.
outsideDelete.inScript: Its text is still in the script.
outsideDelete.inBook: Its text is still in the book.
outsideDelete.noCopy: No copy was kept, so it can only come back from the trash.

restore.title: Restore snapshot?
restore.body:
Replace the files of {name} with the snapshot from {when}? Files created since then go to the trash.

If this vault is open on another device, close Loom Loom there first, or it may write its own copy back.

tutorial.goHereAfterTitle: Once finished with the title, go here

tutorial.createOrOpenAct: Create an act or open an existing one
tutorial.createOrOpenScene: Create a scene or open an existing one
tutorial.sceneIntExt:
Location type completes as you type:
I → INT.
E → EXT.
/ → INT./EXT.
S → EST.
tutorial.sceneLocation: Locations and Sublocations are entities of their own, created automatically when you write their name during scene creation. We will check them later.
tutorial.locationRegion:
Locations can be gathered under regions.
Regions are optional but help organise your world.
tutorial.locationNotes: Each page has its own Notes field. It doesn't go into the script and lives only in your vault.
tutorial.locationItems: You might want to associate specific items with specific locations or characters. You can do it here.
tutorial.locationSublocations: Your locations might have sublocations, for example HOUSE, KITCHEN and HOUSE, BATHROOM.
tutorial.locationRelationships:
Entities have this section so you can build custom connections.
For example, open DEMETER's character page and add a relationship:
[Identifier = Daughter] [Target note = PERSEPHONE]
Then go to PERSEPHONE's page and add:
[Identifier = Mother] [Target note = DEMETER]
tutorial.graphDetour: Before the graph, let's make sure there's something connected: add a scene to an act
tutorial.graphDetourNoAct: Before the graph, let's make sure there's something connected: create an act, then a scene in it
tutorial.openGraph: Let's see how it all connects
tutorial.graphSelect: Click any node to see what it's connected to.
tutorial.graphPanel: Its connections are listed here. Double-click a node to open its page.
tutorial.graphBack: Now go back to the graph
tutorial.graphFocus: Press and hold a node to zoom in on it.
tutorial.graphDrag: Drag a node somewhere else and let go: it springs back to where its connections pull it.
tutorial.graphPin: Now drag it again, and while still holding, right-click. It stays where you put it.
tutorial.graphUnpin: Right-click a pinned node to let it go.
tutorial.graphFilter: Hide or dim whole entity types, or focus on a few entities.
tutorial.graphFilterInside: Focus on entities shows only what's connected to the ones you pick.
tutorial.graphViews: Save the current filter, focus and pins as a view to come back to.
tutorial.graphTimeline: Open the timeline: your {anchors} and {beats} in order.
tutorial.graphTimelineClose: Explore your timeline: {anchors} in order, their {beats} beneath. Close it when you're done.
tutorial.graphAnimate: Replay how your world grew, in the order things were created.
tutorial.graphCreate: Right-click empty space to create a new entity right here.
